part1_fy_stage_table.explicit_non_conflation_note: These are three DIFFERENT sets, not one 'zero-coverage' set. downloaded=0 (8 FYs) is a strict subset of mda_located=0 (9 FYs), which is a strict subset of accepted=0 (10 FYs). FY2011 is in accepted=0 and NOT in downloaded=0 or mda_located=0 (it had 1 download, 1 identity-verify, 1 mda-locate, but 0 accepts). FY2015 is in accepted=0 and mda_located=0 but NOT in downloaded=0 (it had 2 downloads, 0 identity-verifies, 0 mda-locates, 0 accepts). The earlier informal summary '8 of 16 fiscal years at zero' is EXACTLY the downloaded=0 count (8), and is true only for that specific stage -- it is false if read as accepted=0 (which is 10) or mda_located=0 (which is 9).
part1_fy_stage_table.monotonicity_note: coverage.json's own monotonicity_checks show mda_located<=identity_verified is FALSE (12 violations, e.g. INE007A01025::FY2012 'mda_located_without_identity_verified'). MDA location and identity verification are not a strict nested waterfall in this pipeline; an observation can have mda_located=True while identity_verified=False. Transition-loss figures below can therefore be negative (a 'gain') for the identity->MDA step, and that is a real property of the data, not a computation error.
part1_fy_stage_table.transition_losses_definition: loss_X_to_Y = count(X) - count(Y) at the same FY, exactly as pm5_stage_table.csv aggregates it; a negative value means Y > X for that FY (see monotonicity_note).

part2_fy_pattern.classification: CLUSTERED. Not contiguous overall, not alternating, not a single pre/post-date split. Three tight nonzero clusters ({2011-13}/{2012-13}, {2017-18}, {2024-25} depending on stage) separated by multi-year zero runs, with the 2019-2023 gap being the largest single contiguous zero-download run in the whole series.

alignment_checks.era_definition_version: NOT aligned. E1(2010-2012), E4(2016-2019) and E6(2023-2025) are each internally mixed zero/nonzero at the downloaded stage, so era boundaries do not explain the split.
alignment_checks.source_type: NOT aligned. All 3 FY-level zero/nonzero groups are dominated by the same discovery source (nse, priority 10) in the frozen manifests; source type is a per-company-year attribute, not an FY-level one, so it cannot by itself produce an FY-level pattern.
alignment_checks.exchange: NOT aligned. exchange='both' for effectively all sampled large/mid-cap rows regardless of FY group; exchange is a per-company attribute, structurally incapable of producing an FY-level pattern on its own.

part6_historical_vs_current_evidence.explicit_rule_followed: These two classes are never merged into a single 'this is what happened' statement anywhere in this report.

part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.why_separate_clients: cmd_discover and cmd_fetch are separate CLI subcommands ('arpipe discover' then 'arpipe fetch'), documented in cli.py's own module docstring as deliberately decoupled ('Stages are separate commands on purpose... fetch runs once'). discover.nse_session() is called once inside cmd_discover and closed at the end of that command (finally: nse_cl.close()). cmd_fetch is a later, separate process/invocation that only ever reads the discovery manifest file from disk (a JSONL of ReportRef rows: url/source/priority/company_id/fy_end/declared_name/... -- no header or cookie fields exist in that schema) and builds its OWN httpx.Client from scratch at cli.py line 176-177.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q1_why_separate_clients: Architectural: discover and fetch are separate CLI commands/processes so that `extract` can be re-run without re-fetching; there is no shared in-memory client by design, and the on-disk manifest handoff format has no field to carry session state even if the processes were merged.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q2_cookies_differ: YES. discover.nse_session() performs 2 GETs to NSE_HOME to populate its client's cookie jar before any API call. cmd_fetch's client is constructed fresh with no seeding requests; its cookie jar is empty for the life of the command.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q3_headers_differ: YES. discover.NSE_HEADERS = User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language, Referer (pointed at the corporate-filings-annual-reports page). cmd_fetch's client sets only {'User-Agent': discover.UA} -- no Accept, no Accept-Language, no Referer.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q4_user_agent_differs: NO. Both clients use the identical string discover.UA.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q5_redirects_differ: NO. Both rely on httpx's follow_redirects=True with the library default max_redirects (20); neither cli.py nor fetch.py overrides it.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q6_timeout_differs: YES, nominally. discover.nse_session(timeout=20.0) default vs cmd_fetch's httpx.Client(timeout=120). In practice fetch.py's fetch_one() overrides the per-request timeout to 120.0 explicitly on its own call regardless of the client's default, so this difference only matters for calls made directly on the discovery client (which never requests the archive host in production).
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q7_tls_proxy_differs: NO EVIDENCE OF DIFFERENCE. Neither client configures a custom SSL context or proxy; both use httpx defaults.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q8_connection_session_reuse_differs: YES. discover's nse_session() client persists across ALL companies within one `arpipe discover` run (opened once, reused ~2568 times, closed once). cmd_fetch's client persists across all pairs within one `arpipe fetch` run but is a DIFFERENT object with no shared history; there is no code path connecting the two.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q9_discovery_state_transferred_to_fetch: NO. Confirmed structurally, not just observed: the manifest file discover writes (ReportRef JSON rows) has no field for cookies, headers, or session identifiers, and cmd_fetch never reads anything but that file plus its own fresh client. Even if both commands ran in the same process, the current code has no line that would copy cookies/headers from one client to the other.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q10_response_formats_accepted: fetch_one() does not check the Content-Type header at all. It inspects the first 2 bytes of the body: b'PK' is treated as a zip (extracts the largest embedded PDF); anything else is written to disk and opened directly with pymupdf as a PDF. If pymupdf.open() raises, it tries a qpdf repair pass; if that also fails, fetch_one returns None silently (no exception, no WARN/ERR print at that specific point -- the aggregate 'FAILED ... across all candidate sources' print only fires later, in cli.py's ThreadPoolExecutor loop, once every candidate for that pair has been exhausted).
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q11_network_exception_handling: fetch_one() wraps the GET/stream in a broad `except Exception`, stores it as last_err, sleeps 2*(attempt+1) seconds, and retries up to `retries` (default 3) times; after exhausting attempts it re-raises last_err. Separately, HTTP 403/429/503 responses trigger `time.sleep(5*(attempt+1)**2)` and `continue` WITHOUT setting last_err. CONCRETE GAP FOUND: if all `retries` attempts return 403/429/503 (never a generic exception), the for loop exits with last_err still None, and fetch_one falls through to `return None` -- no exception is ever raised, and no information about the repeated 403/429/503 survives anywhere, not even a print statement. This is a genuine, code-verified silent-failure path distinct from the already-known stderr-only WARN/ERR path.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q12_exceptions_persisted_or_printed: Only printed, never persisted. cli.py's _fetch_pair prints a one-line WARN to stderr per exception; the ThreadPoolExecutor loop prints ERR or FAILED to stderr once per pair after all candidates are exhausted. fetch.py itself prints informational [FETCH] lines to STDOUT (zip-extract, repair, decrypt notices) which are a separate channel again. None of these three print channels are written to documents.jsonl, to any log file, or to any other structure that a later reconciliation pass (e.g. tools/pm5_coverage.py) could read. This is confirmed independently by tools/pm5_coverage.py's own source comment (line ~68-71 in the pm5-coverage-funnel worktree): DISCOVERY and DOWNLOAD failures are hard-coded to REASON_CODE_MISSING because, in the tool's own words, those stages have no persisted reason/artifact to inspect -- consistent with, and independently corroborating, the code-reading finding here.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.q13_fetch_step_skipped_before_invocation: Checked directly against the only committed fetch-input-shaped file in this repo, cohort_fetch_manifest.jsonl (460 rows / 194 distinct (company_id, fy_end) pairs, committed at 1d7dc05, 2026-09-11T16:21:07+05:30). This set is EXACTLY equal to the 194 downloaded=True pairs in pm5_stage_table.csv (same FY distribution: {2011:1,2012:28,2013:29,2015:2,2017:31,2018:31,2024:36,2025:36}), and the generating script is not committed. HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND REJECTED: this file is NOT a pre-fetch input that filtered out the 318 candidates before cmd_fetch ran -- it cannot be, because a pre-fetch filter would have had to predict which 194 of 512 candidates would later succeed, which is not something any committed code does. It is far more consistent with being a POST-hoc derivative built FROM the successful documents.jsonl/store contents (the same 2026-09-11 16:21 commit also added tools/seed_historical_labels.py, which reads arpipe/p11_store/documents.jsonl -- the post-fetch success store -- for an unrelated P13b evaluation/labelling task). Within cmd_fetch itself, the only skip logic is the `done` set built from any PRE-EXISTING documents.jsonl in the output root; it skips pairs already recorded as successfully downloaded, and would NOT skip a pair that had only ever failed (failures are never written to documents.jsonl, so they can never appear in `done`). No skip-before-invocation bug was found for the 318 losses; this specific control-flow hypothesis is RULED OUT by direct evidence, not merely unconfirmed.
part7_committed_fetch_control_flow.would_head_accept_todays_responses: Yes for all 10 sampled URLs today (all returned clean 200s with correct magic numbers); fetch_one() would accept and store every one of them without retry.

part9_controlled_differential_test.hypothesis_tested: The fetch-client's missing NSE session cookies/Referer (vs the discovery-client's) causes nsearchives.nseindia.com to block/reset archive downloads.

config_A.description: discovery-client-equivalent: cookie jar seeded by 2 sequential GETs to https://www.nseindia.com and the NSE Referer page, headers = User-Agent + Accept + Accept-Language + Referer, timeout=20s (nse_session() default), follow_redirects=True
config_A.cookie_values: <REDACTED - Akamai bot-management session tokens, not authentication credentials, redacted per Part 5>

config_B.description: fetch-client-equivalent, same as Part 4 config B

part9_controlled_differential_test.aggregate_outcome: A and B both succeed (for all 3 URLs tested, on 2026-09-17 between 13:59:51Z and 14:00:25Z)
part9_controlled_differential_test.response_header_comparison: Byte-for-byte identical response headers from the target host between config A and config B (aside from the Date timestamp and the per-request Akamai-GRN request ID), including the absence of any Set-Cookie header from the archive host itself in either config.
part9_controlled_differential_test.interpretation_current_observation_only: Today, a completely cookie-less, Referer-less client (config B, i.e. what cmd_fetch actually sends) succeeds against nsearchives.nseindia.com exactly as well as a client carrying NSE session cookies and Referer (config A). The archive host shows no observable current-day preference for either configuration. This WEAKENS the cookie/session-asymmetry hypothesis as a general, always-true explanation, without eliminating the possibility that cookies mattered under the specific (unobserved) conditions of the 2026-09-11 run.
part9_controlled_differential_test.explicit_caveat: This is a CURRENT differential result. It shows a reproducible current mechanism (or lack thereof). It does NOT automatically prove that cookie/session state did or did not cause the historical 2026-09-11 losses -- that would require historical attempt-level evidence, which part8 establishes does not exist.

part11_historical_timestamp_analysis.source: pm5_source_snapshots/live_store_documents.jsonl 'fetched_at' field (frozen, read-only), as already extracted by reports/pc0_diagnostic_base_check.json step1_fiscal_year_pattern.fetched_at_timestamp_clustering
part11_historical_timestamp_analysis.field_semantics: fetched_at is generated client-side by arpipe/models.py's StoredDoc dataclass (default_factory=dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).isoformat()), stamped at the moment fetch.py's fetch_one() successfully constructs a StoredDoc -- i.e. AFTER the GET succeeded, the zip/pdf was parsed or repaired, and the blob was written to the content-addressed store. It exists ONLY on success; no equivalent field is stamped anywhere on failure.
what_it_proves: All 194 successful downloads completed between 2026-09-11T10:28:44.383654+00:00 and 2026-09-11T10:33:08.081915+00:00 (a ~4.5 minute span).

Within that span, successes cluster into 3 tight sub-bursts by FY, in order: {2012,2013} first (10:28:44-10:29:58), {2017,2018} next (10:30:04-10:31:26), {2024,2025} last (10:31:29-10:33:08), with FY2011's single success (10:29:04) landing inside the first burst's window and FY2015's 2 successes (10:31:21-10:31:22) landing inside the second burst's window.
This is consistent with 3 sub-populations of company-years each becoming fetchable in a short window, rather than 3 separate crawl days -- it is one continuous span.
what_it_does_not_prove: That any of the 318 failed pairs were attempted during this window, before it, after it, or at all -- no timestamp of any kind exists for them.
How many attempts (of the up-to-3 built into fetch_one's retry loop) preceded each successful StoredDoc construction -- attempt count is not persisted.

That there was only ONE invocation of `arpipe fetch` ever run against this cohort -- cmd_fetch supports incremental resume via a `done' set read from any pre-existing documents.jsonl, so multiple invocations over time are structurally possible and would leave no trace for any invocation that produced zero successes.

Ordering/causality between the sub-bursts beyond 'these particular successes completed in this order' -- e.g. it does not prove the FY2012/2013 candidates were attempted before the FY2024/2025 candidates, only that they finished first (ThreadPoolExecutor runs pairs concurrently, so completion order is not the same as attempt-start order).
part11_historical_timestamp_analysis.explicit_rule_followed: This diagnosis does NOT infer 'not downloaded = attempted and failed' from this timestamp evidence. For the 318 losses, historical invocation remains UNKNOWN per part8.

where_code_logs_vs_swallows.prints_to_stderr: cli.py cmd_fetch's _fetch_pair (WARN line per exception) and the ThreadPoolExecutor completion loop (ERR / FAILED lines).
where_code_logs_vs_swallows.prints_to_stdout: fetch.py's fetch_one (zip-extract / repair / decrypt notices via bare print()).
where_code_logs_vs_swallows.swallows_silently_no_print_at_all: fetch_one's own exhausted-403/429/503 path (part7 q11) -- falls through to `return None` with last_err still None, zero output on any channel.
where_code_logs_vs_swallows.persists_a_structured_reason_to_a_file: Nowhere in the DOWNLOAD or DISCOVERY stages. IDENTITY and ACCEPTANCE stages DO have inspectable fields in the post-processing manifest (verify.py/triage.py's downstream outputs) that tools/pm5_coverage.py can read after the fact -- this is why those two stages show 100% / 90.7% reason coverage while DOWNLOAD/DISCOVERY show 0%.

part12_observability_gap.structural_root_of_the_gap: It is not merely that fetch.py/cli.py choose stderr over a log file. It is that a DOWNLOAD failure produces NO ARTIFACT of any kind (the content-addressed store only ever writes an entry on success), so even a smart post-hoc reconciliation tool has nothing on disk to inspect for a failed pair. tools/pm5_coverage.py's own source comment confirms this design tension directly: DISCOVERY and DOWNLOAD failures are unconditionally coded REASON_CODE_MISSING because those two stages have no persisted artifact to derive a reason from.

separation_maintained.observability_failure_confirmed: YES, directly, by code reading: DOWNLOAD/DISCOVERY failure reasons are never persisted anywhere, only ever printed (or, in one code path, not even printed).
separation_maintained.acquisition_failure_mechanism_confirmed: NOT by this fact alone. 'Reason was not persisted' proves the pipeline cannot currently tell you WHY a given company-year failed. It does not by itself tell you WHAT that reason was. The two are reported separately throughout this diagnosis and must not be merged.

primary_cause.category: C. HTTP/access problem (time-varying availability on the NSE archive host)
supporting_evidence: Frozen historical evidence: all 194 successes fall inside one ~4.5 minute window with 3 internal sub-bursts, nothing before or after (part11).

Current-observation evidence: the identical 10-URL sample flipped from 0/10 success (pc0_diagnostic_base_check.md Step 3, same day) to 10/10 success (this task's part4) within roughly 40-50 minutes, on the same network, with no code changes in between.

part10: no structural (URL/host/path/extension/source/exchange) difference was found between the DOWNLOAD_ZERO_FY and control groups, in either the frozen evidence or today's live probing -- ruling out a company- or file-specific explanation and leaving a time-dependent access condition as the best-supported remaining explanation.

part9's controlled differential test found NO current requirement for discovery-session cookies/Referer to succeed against this host -- ruling out client-configuration asymmetry as a SOLE or CURRENT explanation (it may still be a contributing factor under conditions not observed today; see contributing_factors).
why_not_high_confidence: Historical per-attempt execution evidence for the 318 losses does not exist (part8: UNKNOWN). This diagnosis cannot directly observe that a 403/429/503/timeout/reset actually occurred for any specific one of the 318 pairs on 2026-09-11. The conclusion rests on convergent circumstantial evidence (timestamp clustering + demonstrated current volatility + absence of any structural alternative), which this task's own confidence definitions place at MEDIUM, not HIGH.

contributing_factors.role: Does not cause the acquisition loss, but makes it impossible to confirm or refute the primary-cause hypothesis directly from historical records, and would silently absorb the same failure again on any future re-run.

contributing_factors.factor: fetch_one's silent-return-None path on exhausted 403/429/503 (part7 q11)
contributing_factors.role: A confirmed, code-level gap that specifically matches an HTTP/access-problem failure mode (repeated 403/429/503) with total silence -- directly compatible with, though not proof of, the primary cause.

contributing_factors.factor: Discovery-client vs fetch-client configuration asymmetry (part7 q1-q9, part9)
contributing_factors.role: A real, confirmed code asymmetry (cookies, Referer, Accept headers all differ). Tested directly and found NOT to matter under today's conditions (part9: A and B both succeed). Downgraded from primary-cause candidate to a documented-but-unconfirmed contributing hypothesis; cannot be fully ruled out for 2026-09-11's specific unobserved conditions.

causes_considered_and_ruled_out.hypothesis: D. File-format/validation problem (e.g. fetch_one rejecting a valid file)
causes_considered_and_ruled_out.status: RULED OUT for the sampled URLs -- all 10 sample URLs, including all 5 DOWNLOAD_ZERO_FY ones, returned valid, correctly-typed ZIP/PDF bodies today with correct magic numbers; fetch_one's format handling would accept every one of them.

causes_considered_and_ruled_out.hypothesis: E. Control-flow/skipping problem (candidates dropped between discovery and fetch invocation)
causes_considered_and_ruled_out.status: RULED OUT for the specific committed-manifest hypothesis tested in part7 q13 (cohort_fetch_manifest.jsonl) -- shown to be a post-hoc derivative of successful downloads, not a pre-fetch filter. cmd_fetch's own `done`-set skip logic only skips already-succeeded pairs, never failed ones. No other skip mechanism was found in the read code.

NOT APPLICABLE to this loss -- by definition, all 318 losses in this diagnosis have discovered=True; a discovery-stage problem is a separate, already-quantified loss (64 company-years, DISCOVERED stage, out of scope for 'discover->download' specifically).

part13_root_cause_structure.multiple_primary_causes_note: Only one primary cause (C) is supported by convergent evidence strong enough to name as primary; B (fetch invocation/client-state) is retained only as a contributing/unconfirmed factor per the evidence in part9, not promoted to a second primary cause.

part14_confidence_definitions.HIGH: Direct evidence from committed control flow or persisted historical records.
part14_confidence_definitions.MEDIUM: Multiple independent pieces of evidence converge, but historical execution cannot be directly observed.
part14_confidence_definitions.LOW: Plausible explanation with incomplete supporting evidence.

HIGH: Discovery-client vs fetch-client code asymmetry exists (direct code reading).
DOWNLOAD/DISCOVERY reason-code coverage is 0% (direct, persisted frozen evidence).
fetch_one's exhausted-403/429/503 path returns None with no exception and no output (direct code reading).
cohort_fetch_manifest.jsonl's pair-set equals the downloaded=True set exactly, ruling out the pre-fetch-filter hypothesis (direct, computed evidence).
MEDIUM: PRIMARY CAUSE: time-varying HTTP/access condition on the NSE archive host explains the discover->download loss pattern.
LOW: Any claim about what specifically happened (timeout vs reset vs 403 vs something else) to any INDIVIDUAL one of the 318 lost pairs on 2026-09-11 -- there is no evidence at that granularity at all.

unresolved_questions: Whether the 2026-09-11 crawl(s) ran on code byte-identical to HEAD 0fb8cbf (cannot be established from committed history or frozen evidence alone).
Whether there was exactly one `arpipe fetch` invocation on 2026-09-11 or several (documents.jsonl's append + resume-skip design cannot distinguish these).
What specific failure mode (timeout / reset / 403 / 429 / 503 / other) applied to any specific one of the 318 losses -- no per-attempt evidence exists.

Whether the NSE archive host's volatility is genuinely time-of-day/session/rate-limit-state dependent on NSE's side, or reflects transient conditions specific to the IIT Kanpur campus network used for all live probing in this diagnosis and its predecessor -- both explanations remain open.

Whether concurrency (ThreadPoolExecutor worker count) during the historical run interacted with per-host rate limiting or Akamai bot-mitigation thresholds -- HostLimiter enforces only a 1.5s per-host minimum interval, which would not by itself prevent a burst of concurrent connections from multiple worker threads to the same host at the moment the limiter's window opens.

minimal_next_repair_test.description: Before any repair: add structured, persisted failure-reason logging to cmd_fetch/_fetch_pair and fetch_one (e.g. write a JSONL row per failed attempt with company_id, fy_end, source, url, exception type/message or HTTP status, and a UTC timestamp) -- purely additive observability, no retry/backoff/timeout/client changes. Then re-run `arpipe fetch` against a SMALL, already-frozen subset of the discover->download losses (e.g. this task's 5 DOWNLOAD_ZERO_FY sample observations) in isolation, and inspect the new persisted reasons directly. This converts 'historical invocation = UNKNOWN' into a directly observable, persisted, per-attempt record for future runs, without touching acquisition logic, and would immediately confirm or refute whether repeated 403/429/503 (part7 q11's silent path), timeouts, or resets are actually what these specific pairs hit.
minimal_next_repair_test.why_this_and_not_a_bigger_fix: This task's evidence supports MEDIUM confidence in a time-varying access condition, not HIGH confidence in any single deterministic bug. Adding retries, backoff, or cookie-sharing now (part9's ruled-out-as-necessary hypothesis) would be a repair attempt without the observability needed to verify it worked or understand why. The logging-only step is the smallest change that converts an UNKNOWN into evidence, consistent with this task's scope (diagnosis only, no repair).
